sections.overview: Calvert’s emerald is a rare, range-restricted dragonfly recorded mainly in the Florida Panhandle and nearby southeastern states.
sections.identification: It is an emerald dragonfly in the family Corduliidae.
sections.habitat: Florida surveys have recorded adults around seepage streams and sandhill forest.
sections.diet: The species sources consulted do not provide a verified prey list.
sections.behavior: Most field records concern adults; species-specific daily behavior remains poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: Its nymph has not been collected in the field, so its breeding microhabitat remains unconfirmed.
sections.ecology: A recent review suggests seepage streams beside intact sandhill forest as likely breeding habitat, but labels this an inference.
sections.conservation: The latest IUCN assessment located lists it as Data Deficient.
